intro: Professionals and everyday users convert kilopascals (kPa) to psi (psi) when working across metric and imperial standards in automotive tire inflation placards, hydraulic cylinder design, scuba diving tanks, and barometric weather tracking. One kilopascal equals 0.145038 psi, while 1 pounds per square inch equals 6.894757 kilopascals. Whether you are verifying pressure specifications on imported equipment, cross-checking technical datasheets, or scaling practical measurements, this converter applies the exact NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 reference relationship with instant precision.

mistakesAndEdgeCases.title: Gauge Pressure (psig) vs. Absolute Pressure (psia)
items: This converter scales pressure magnitude directly between kPa and psi. In automotive tires, HVAC, and compressed air systems, gauges display Gauge Pressure (referenced to ambient atmospheric pressure, ~14.696 psi or 101.325 kPa at sea level).
For thermodynamic gas laws (PV = nRT) or vacuum chamber calculations, convert gauge pressure to absolute pressure by adding local barometric pressure before scaling.

faqs.question: How many psi (psi) are in 1 kilopascal (kPa)?
faqs.answer: There are 0.14503774 psi (psi) in 1 kilopascal (kPa), which rounds to 0.145 psi for everyday calculations. Conversely, 1 pounds per square inch equals 6.894757 kilopascals.

faqs.question: How do I convert kilopascals to psi (kPa to psi)?
faqs.answer: To convert kilopascals to psi, use the formula: psi = kPa × 0.14503774. For example, converting 240 kPa gives 34.8091 psi.

faqs.question: What is 240 kilopascals in psi?
faqs.answer: 240 kilopascals (kPa) equals exactly 34.8091 psi (psi) using standard NIST SP 811 and ISO 80000 conversion factors.
